name: Binnui
overview: Binnui was a male Levite recognized for his role in the restoration of Jerusalem's walls, specifically repairing a section as recorded in Nehemiah 3:24. He is also mentioned among the Levites who sealed the covenant document in Nehemiah 10:9, indicating his involvement in the communal religious renewal. His contributions highlight the active participation of the tribe of Levi in both physical and spiritual restoration during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Binnui means "son," reflecting a common Hebrew proper name without a specific divine attribution. This simple meaning aligns with the typical naming conventions of the time and is directly referenced in Nehemiah 3:24.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Binnui as the son of Henadad, establishing a clear paternal relationship in Nehemiah 3:24. Beyond this, no additional family connections are recorded for him.
scriptureSignificance: Binnui's significance lies in his role as a Levite who actively participated in the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls, a critical act of faith and obedience in the restoration era. His inclusion on the sealed covenant document underscores his commitment to the renewed covenant community under God's guidance. Together, these details emphasize his faithful service in both the physical and spiritual restoration of Israel.
